blocks.text: Production bugs involving **Recursive types and depth limits** rarely look like syntax errors — they show up as wrong data, memory growth, flaky tests, or CI type failures. blocks.body: Treating Recursive types and depth limits as pure syntax without compile-time or run-time behavior. Skipping validation at API/JSON boundaries. Ignoring strict compiler flags differences. Hand-waving in design review without a test or metric.

blocks.text: Prove mastery of **Recursive types and depth limits** with a failing test that captures the edge case, a DevTools or heap snapshot showing the bug, and a clear tradeoff statement in design review. Senior interviewers want mechanism — what the compiler and emitted JS actually do — plus when the simple explicit version beats the clever abstraction.
